headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: Cline’s browser/files/MCP outputs can be fed into OpenMetadata’s MCP/API workflows, creating unsafe default trust and mutable-resource conflicts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP; OpenMetadata exposes MCP/APIs/webhooks. That creates a plausible bridge where Cline-generated content can be consumed by OpenMetadata or vice versa. The profiles do not prove direct parsing of each other’s outputs, so I avoid high, but the shared filesystem/MCP surfaces make injection plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF Cline writes attacker-controlled text into workspace files that OpenMetadata ingests via MCP/API, injection is possible.
IF OpenMetadata emits content that Cline later treats as instructions, the bridge becomes exploitable.
mitigations: Disable shared workspace ingestion paths.
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent files.
Restrict OpenMetadata MCP methods to read-only for the pair.
Add a manual review step before Cline forwards any OpenMetadata output.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate workspaces or containers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress; OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data and exposes APIs/webhooks/MCP. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive metadata can flow from one to the other. The profiles do not show a guaranteed shared store, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or secrets store, leakage risk increases.
IF OpenMetadata sends catalog content through APIs/webhooks while Cline has network egress, data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate credentials for each agent.
Block Cline from reading OpenMetadata secrets or governance exports.
Limit OpenMetadata API responses to minimum necessary fields.
Turn off webhook forwarding for shared datasets.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls between the agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem, modify git state, and execute shell commands; OpenMetadata can act through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Both can mutate shared resources, and the profiles show no locking or coordination primitive. That makes concurrent writes and state corruption plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repo or workspace, conflicting writes can occur.
IF OpenMetadata updates shared metadata while Cline edits files derived from it, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate directories or repos.
Pause one agent before the other mutates shared state.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Add a lock file around shared resources.
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination for shared metadata and git operations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived facts, and file edits; OpenMetadata is built around governance, lineage, and trust metadata and can act via APIs/webhooks/MCP. If OpenMetadata treats Cline output as authoritative, errors can cascade into catalog or governance actions. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests Cline-produced facts without validation, incorrect lineage or governance records can propagate.
IF Cline consumes OpenMetadata outputs as ground truth, downstream edits may be based on stale metadata.
mitigations: Require human verification before catalog updates.
Compare Cline outputs against source-of-truth systems.
Mark all inter-agent outputs as untrusted by default.
Add checksum or schema validation on exchanged artifacts.
requires-engineering: build a verification workflow before any automated action.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata explicitly handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data, while Cline handles source code and browser screenshots and stores model-provider API keys. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so I cannot claim a concrete breach, but the mixed data classes and API/webhook exposure create a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated data is routed through the pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into OpenMetadata and then forwarded through APIs/webhooks, policy mismatch may occur.
IF Cline processes screenshots or code containing regulated content, retention and access controls must match the governing policy.
mitigations: Classify data before either agent touches it.
Disable retention of screenshots and exported metadata.
Restrict regulated datasets to approved environments only.
Review vendor residency and DPA terms before use.
requires-engineering: align logging and retention policies across both systems.
